findings.desc: BLOCKER: canStartDevGuard returns true early at 'if (!policy.plan.requireStoryReview) return true' (line 412) BEFORE the parallel-decomposition sub-check (line 425). A profile that does not require story_review (e.g. light) bypasses the hard gate entirely — a story asserting false parallelism under mode=block can enter DEV despite a real overlap. getGuardFailureReason's parallel branch runs unconditionally, so it still reports the block => decision/message PARITY also breaks (guard allows, reason blocks). Fix: restructure so only the review-record checks are gated on requireStoryReview; the fail-open parallel sub-check ALWAYS runs before return true. Add a light-profile + mode=block smoke case.
findings.resolvedReason: canStartDevGuard restructured: review-record checks gated inside if(requireStoryReview){}, the early return-true removed; the fail-open parallel sub-check now runs on EVERY PLAN->DEV entry regardless of review policy. commit 485eba1a8.

findings.desc: MAJOR: the review-gate refactor changed 'return (blockerCount ?? issueCount) === 0' (strict zero) into 'if ((blockerCount ?? issueCount) > 0) return false' (line 420) — NOT behavior-equivalent. A signed review with a non-numeric/negative/missing count (e.g. blockerCount=-1, or string '0') is NOT > 0 so it now PASSES the review gate, where the original strict ===0 rejected anything other than numeric zero. getGuardFailureReason line ~819 has the same '> 0' (pre-existing) so for parity both must use strict !==0. Fix: const gateCount = blockerCount ?? issueCount; if (gateCount !== 0) return false; in canStartDevGuard, and !==0 in getGuardFailureReason's review-count check.
findings.resolvedReason: strict !==0 at both sites (canStartDevGuard line ~437 + getGuardFailureReason review-reason ~845), restoring the original ===0 semantics (negative/NaN/odd counts no longer pass). commit 485eba1a8.

findings.desc: MAJOR (express-channel bypass): the parallel hard-block is enforced ONLY by canStartDevGuard on PLAN->DEV. The INIT_CHECK->DEV express channel is guarded by canSkipPlanGuard (machine.ts ~433-446) which NEVER calls parallelDecompositionEnforcedBlock. So a quickPath story (small checklist, no risk signals) reaches DEV with a provable overlap/broad-glob/unreadable-peer block under mode=block WITHOUT refusal — the gate's core property (a provable contradiction blocks DEV entry) is violated on the express door. Also a phantom-message site (getGuardFailureReason renders a parallel message the express guard never enforced). Fix: add the same fail-open parallel sub-check to canSkipPlanGuard; add an express (INIT_CHECK phase) + mode=block + overlap smoke asserting the guard refuses + the reason renders.
findings.resolvedReason: added the same fail-open parallel sub-check to canSkipPlanGuard (INIT_CHECK->DEV express door); getGuardFailureReason tracks tookExpressChannel and skips the inapplicable review-record reason for an express story so it surfaces the real parallel-decomposition reason. The gate is now enforced on BOTH doors. commit 485eba1a8.

findings.desc: MINOR x2: formatParallelDecompositionBlock's overlap recompute (~353-364) and peer_contract_unreadable_parallel recompute (~385-398) select the named peer by filtering only parallelSafe!=='yes', omitting the gate's active-peer filter (!TERMINAL_PHASES.has(phase)). So the message can name a DONE/DISCARDED parallelSafe=yes peer that sorts earlier in listStoryIds() while the gate's block came from a different ACTIVE peer — misleading remediation text. Fix: import TERMINAL_PHASES from parallel-policy.js and skip terminal peers in both recompute loops so the named peer matches the gate's active set.
findings.resolvedReason: formatParallelDecompositionBlock overlap + peer_contract_unreadable recompute loops now skip TERMINAL_PHASES peers (imported from parallel-policy.js), matching the gate activePeers filter, so a terminal peer is never named. commit 485eba1a8.

findings.desc: MINOR (migration hazard, gate is FROZEN/Story-2 so DOCUMENT only): a legacy active peer carrying parallelSafe='yes' but with NO scope-contract.json (never ran scope_contract_set) is absent from the contracts map, so under mode=block the gate fires peer_contract_unreadable_parallel and hard-blocks an UNRELATED self story sharing the wave. This is fail-closed by §4.8 design (closes the corrupt-peer bypass) but is a real migration surprise when flipping mode=block in an existing repo. Out of S5 scope to change the frozen gate; resolve by documenting the hazard (e.g. in the spec/release notes: mode=block requires every active parallelSafe=yes story to carry a scope contract).
findings.resolvedReason: Gate parallel-decomposition-gate.ts is FROZEN (Story 2) so no code change; added a MIGRATION HAZARD comment above parallelDecompositionEnforcedBlock noting mode=block requires every active parallelSafe=yes story to carry a readable scope contract. Documented, intentional §4.8 fail-closed behavior. commit 485eba1a8.

findings.desc: BLOCKER (two more unguarded doors): there are FOUR START->DEV doors (PHASE_EVENT_BY_TARGET DEV:'START'): INIT_CHECK->DEV (canSkipPlanGuard, now guarded), PLAN->DEV (canStartDevGuard, now guarded), and the rollback transitions REVIEW->DEV (machine.ts ~691-693) + TEST->DEV (~702-704) which have START:{target:'DEV'} with NO parallel guard (only cwd-worktree). The gate evaluates self.parallelSafe against active non-terminal peers regardless of self's phase, so a parallelSafe=yes story rolling back from REVIEW/TEST to DEV (the 'Run story_advance DEV to rework' path) while a colliding active peer exists re-enters DEV in violation — same bypass class as the round-1 express finding, on two more doors. Fix: extract ONE shared fail-open parallel-gate check and apply it to ALL FOUR START->DEV edges (add guards to the REVIEW + TEST states' START transitions and mirror in canSendStoryEventWithoutSnapshotCan's REVIEW/TEST cases); extend getGuardFailureReason to render the parallel block message for REVIEW/TEST->DEV sources; add smoke cases for REVIEW->DEV + TEST->DEV blocked (+ disjoint + fail-open companions).
findings.resolvedReason: All FOUR START->DEV doors now enforce the parallel hard-block via one shared fail-open wrapper parallelDevEntryBlock: canStartDevGuard (PLAN) + canSkipPlanGuard (INIT_CHECK express) refactored to use it; new canReenterDevGuard (parallel-only, fail-open) attached as guard 'canReenterDev' to the REVIEW->DEV + TEST->DEV rollback START transitions and mirrored in canSendStoryEventWithoutSnapshotCan; getGuardFailureReason renders the parallel reason on all four doors via isRollbackDoor. Smoke adds REVIEW/TEST rollback enforce+disjoint+fail-open cases. commit 4f36f5c1e.

findings.desc: MINOR: formatParallelDecompositionBlock's overlap recompute (~369-372) uses globsOverlap(...).pairs.find(([a,b])=>a===b), but globsOverlap.pairs includes tier-2 shared-prefix/wildcard matches, so two identical WILDCARD entries (e.g. 'src/x/*'==='src/x/*') match and the message cites a wildcard as a 'literal' collision and can name the WRONG peer (not the tier-1 literal-collision peer the gate actually blocked on). Parity + the block itself stay correct; message actionability only. Fix: mirror the gate's tier-1 literalCollisions logic in the formatter (only entries with no trailing /* or /** that are literally equal in both write-sets) so the named peer/path is the literal collision that drove the block.
findings.resolvedReason: formatParallelDecompositionBlock overlap recompute replaced globsOverlap pairs a===b (which matched tier-2 wildcards) with firstLiteralCollision/isLiteralWriteSetEntry mirroring the gate's literalCollisions/isLiteralPath (literal iff no trailing /* or /**); the message now names only a peer with a genuine tier-1 literal collision. Smoke asserts a wildcard-only peer sorting earlier is NOT named. commit 4f36f5c1e.
